cf.title: create table like including storage parameter

input.subject: create table like including storage parameter

verdict_reasoning: The goal is reasonable, and the open point is how copied reloptions combine with other sources. Per standards-compat-1, folding PARAMETERS into including all makes commands that work today fail with a duplicate parameter error. Per standards-compat-2, the proposal gives no rule for several like sources plus a with clause, the same gap that stalled [P1]. The demand objection (demand-1) is real but would not stop a committer by itself.

brief.title: Add including parameters to create table like
brief.problem: create table ... like copies columns, defaults, constraints, indexes and more, but not the source table's storage parameters (pg_class.reloptions). Users who want a similar table must repeat every storage parameter by hand.
brief.proposed_design: A new like_option PARAMETERS copies the source relation's reloptions, including toast.* options, to the new table, and including all now covers it. Parameters that are also given in the with clause raise a duplicate error. The option is ignored when the source is a view, for create foreign table ... like, and for a partitioned target table.
user_visible_surface: New like_option in create table: { including | excluding } parameters.
including all now also copies table storage parameters.
New keyword PARAMETERS added to the grammar keyword list.
Changed C API in reloptions.h, per the touched-file list; the material does not say what changed.
author_claims: The option saves users from listing every storage parameter by hand.
It makes a table made with like closer to the source table.
Earlier version notes say it applies to matviews as well as tables.
A failure from conflicting parameters across two like clauses is no different from other existing like failures.
brief.thread_state: David Johnston and Nathan Bossart chose the PARAMETERS name, Euler Taveira reviewed the code, and lakshmi tested v9. Fujii Masao's backward compatibility concern about including all with two sources is open after the author's reply.
unclear: What happens when two like sources set the same parameter with equal or different values.
Whether existing scripts using including all now fail when they also give the same parameter in with.
Which C API change in reloptions.h extensions will see.
Whether the docs describe ignoring the option for views, partitioned targets and foreign tables.
Whether pg_dump or other tools that use including all are affected.

prior_attempts.title: create table like: ACCESS METHOD
prior_attempts.who_objected: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Vik Fearing
prior_attempts.quote: Whereas the access method is a table property. So I don't think this syntax is the right approach for this feature.
prior_attempts.reason: LIKE expands to column definitions, but the access method is a table property, so two LIKE clauses with different access methods can conflict. Its interaction with USING is also undefined. The patch overwrote any AM given in USING, and Michael Paquier asked for a clear definition of these corner cases. Peter Eisentraut argued that this syntax is the wrong approach and suggested something like USING (LIKE t1).
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 copied the access method, and this proposal copies reloptions. This one raises an error on a conflict with the with clause, where P1 overwrote USING. It still gives no rule for two like sources.

objections.title: Including all now fails on commands that succeed today
objections.failure_scenario: A deployment script runs create table x (like t1 including all, like t2 including all), and both sources set fillfactor. Another runs create table y (like t including all) with (fillfactor = 90) on a source that already sets fillfactor. Both work on 19. After upgrade both fail with a duplicate parameter error, and the user finds out only when the migration breaks.
objections.argument: Message #16 raises the two-source case, and the brief notes it is still open. Message #17 answers that like can already fail, for example on duplicate columns, but that failure exists today, while this one is new for unchanged commands. Message #1 and the commit message make a parameter given in both with and like an error. The proposal does not consider letting with override copied values, or merging equal values, which would keep existing scripts working.
objections.author_must_show: Why should copied reloptions raise an error instead of yielding to an explicit with clause or to an equal value from another source?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 confirms the duplicate error, and message #17 cites only a failure that exists today. Earlier like options also joined including all, but none made a working command fail.

objections.title: A table-level property copied through a per-source like clause
objections.failure_scenario: A user writes create table x (like hot_table including parameters, like cold_table including parameters), where the two sources set different fillfactor and autovacuum settings. The command fails. The user can only fix it by switching to excluding parameters on one source, and nothing in the docs says which source should win.
objections.argument: Like expands into column-level elements, but reloptions belong to the whole table. [P1] stalled for the same reason with access methods, because two like clauses could conflict and the interaction with USING was not defined. Here the with clause has the same role as USING there. The v10 documentation hunk does not describe conflicts between sources, between a source and with, or the cases where the option is ignored.
objections.author_must_show: What rule decides the outcome when several like sources and the with clause set the same parameter, and where is it documented?

critic.reasoning: [P1] fits: reloptions, like an access method, are single-valued table properties that can conflict across like clauses and with an explicit clause. The thread does not say why the like syntax suits such a property, or what happens with equal values.

objections.title: No user demand shown beyond convenience for one workflow
objections.failure_scenario: The project adds a new keyword and like_option to support it for years. Users who clone tables with custom reloptions already copy pg_class.reloptions into a with clause, or run alter table ... set afterwards. Few people notice the new option, and its cost stays.
objections.argument: No message cites a field report, a -general or -bugs request, or another system that offers this. The case rests on the commit message's claim of convenience, and messages #2 and #5 discuss naming, not need. Reloptions are few and easy to read from pg_class, so a short script covers the gap. A committer would likely ask who has been blocked by this.
objections.author_must_show: Which users or tools clone tables with like today and hit missing reloptions, and why is reading pg_class.reloptions not enough for them?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows no user report or request, and a with clause or alter table ... set does the job today. Two committers engaged without questioning the need, which lowers the weight but does not show demand.

refuted.title: Including all plus a with clause now fails for existing commands
refuted.failure_scenario: A deploy script runs `create table t_new (like t including all) with (fillfactor = 90)`, and t already has fillfactor set. After the upgrade, PARAMETERS is part of including all and duplicates raise an error, so the script fails. The user finds out when a migration that worked before stops on the new release.
refuted.argument: Message #1 states that a parameter given both by LIKE and in the with clause is an error. The patch also folds PARAMETERS into including all. [P1] stalled on the same question: how a table property copied by LIKE combines with the explicit clause, there USING. The thread does not discuss letting with override the copied value, or leaving PARAMETERS out of including all.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should an explicit with value raise an error instead of overriding the copied one, given that existing including all scripts would break?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which covers the with clause case and the two-source case without relying on [P1].

refuted.title: Two like sources with the same parameter break a working command
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs `create table x (like t1 including all, like t2 including all)` where both sources set fillfactor. This works today and fails after the patch, even when both values are equal. The user finds out after upgrading.
refuted.argument: Fujii Masao raised this in message #16. In message #17 the author answered that LIKE can already fail, using duplicate column names as the example. But that case fails today too, so it is not a regression, and the fillfactor case is. [P1] was returned for this reason: a table property placed in a clause that can appear more than once. The proposal gives no rule for equal or differing values.
refuted.author_must_show: What rule decides the result when two like sources set the same parameter, and why is a new failure for including all acceptable?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the same two-source regression from message #16 and the same gap in the reply in message #17.

refuted.title: Generic name PARAMETERS invites later changes to including all
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release extends including parameters to cover column attribute options, as message #10 suggests. Scripts that use including all then start copying n_distinct settings into new tables without any change on the user side. Message #11 says this could cause bad plans, and users would find out only through plan regressions.
refuted.argument: The commit message says the option "may encompass other kind parameters in the table" in the future. Messages #2 and #5 chose the broad name on purpose. Every later extension would change what including all does for existing commands, so the scope needs to be fixed now. The documentation hunk only says "all table parameters, such as" storage parameters, which does not set a limit.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the documentation commit to including parameters meaning pg_class.reloptions only, so that its meaning under including all stays fixed?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a later patch that copies column options, and message #11 already argued against that. This patch copies only pg_class.reloptions, and any wider scope would get its own review.

refuted.title: Including all starts copying reloptions, so existing commands can fail
refuted.failure_scenario: A deploy script runs `create table x (like t including all) with (fillfactor = 90)` against a table that sets fillfactor. Today the command succeeds. After the upgrade it fails with a duplicate-parameter error, and the user finds out when the script breaks in production.
refuted.argument: Message #16 shows that two LIKE sources that both set fillfactor now fail. The single-source case with a WITH clause (message #1) is likely more common. Message #17 answers that LIKE can already fail, but those failures exist today, while this one breaks commands that work now. [P1] stalled on the same point: a table property copied through LIKE conflicts across clauses and with explicit clauses. No merge or precedence rule is given here.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should including all change meaning, rather than leaving parameters out of all or letting an explicit WITH value or the last LIKE source win?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. Its extra question about leaving parameters out of including all belongs with that objection.

refuted.title: Per-relkind silent ignore rules will drift as reloptions change
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds storage parameters for partitioned tables or a new relkind. The skip rule in the LIKE code still drops them, no test fails, and users silently get tables without the parameters they asked for.
refuted.argument: The skip rules were added one case at a time, after test failures: views in message #12, partitioned targets in message #15, and foreign tables in message #9. Each future reloption change must remember this list, and nothing fails loudly if it is missed. The commit message also says PARAMETERS may later cover other kinds of parameters, so the scope stays open. The documentation hunk for v10 does not mention any of the ignore cases.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the rule be written as copying whatever the target relkind accepts, so a future reloption change cannot silently skip parameters without a test failing?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a future change, such as reloptions for partitioned tables or a new relkind, that the proposal does not include. The missing documentation of the ignore cases is a docs matter, outside levels 1-2.

refuted.title: Including all users pay for a gain only some of them want
refuted.failure_scenario: A migration script runs create table ... (like t1 including all, like t2 including all), and both sources set fillfactor. It succeeds today and fails after upgrade with a duplicate parameter error. A script that also gives fillfactor in with fails the same way, and the user finds out only when the deploy breaks.
refuted.argument: Message #16 raises the two-source case, and message #17 answers that like can already fail. That answer covers failures that exist today, not ones the patch adds to statements that work now. The users who want reloptions copied could opt in with including parameters, but folding the option into including all moves the risk onto everyone. [P1] stalled on the same conflict between two like clauses for a table property.
refuted.author_must_show: Why must including all cover parameters when users who want them can write including parameters, and how do existing including all scripts keep working?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1: same two failing commands, same reading of messages #16 and #17. The who-pays framing adds no new scenario.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes src/include/access/reloptions.h, and the material does not say what extensions will see.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a non-standard like_option and a new keyword PARAMETERS to the grammar.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Including all changes meaning for unchanged commands, so some scripts that work on the old release fail after upgrade.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new keyword, a conflict rule, and skip rules for views, foreign tables and partitioned targets must be kept in step with reloptions.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: Users can already copy pg_class.reloptions into a with clause or run alter table ... set afterwards.

questions: What is the result when two like sources set the same parameter, with equal values and with different values?
Why does a parameter given in the with clause raise an error instead of overriding the value copied by like?
Why must including all cover PARAMETERS, when users who want reloptions copied can write including parameters?
Which users or tools clone tables with like today and are blocked by missing reloptions?
What changes in reloptions.h, and does it affect extensions that call the existing reloptions functions?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the create table like parse code and reloptions. Fujii Masao raised the open compatibility concern in message #16, and Nathan Bossart removed himself as reviewer in the CommitFest history.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the new keyword, the conflict rule, and the changed meaning of including all, with no end date because scripts depend on it.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted ten versions over about a year, kept the entry rebased across six CommitFests, and replied to the concern in message #17.

priority.reason: The patch is about 19 KiB in the parser and reloptions code and adds one keyword, but the thread shows no user request. The conflict rule and the including all behaviour need agreement before more code review helps.

provisional_note: Without the code, the reloptions.h change, the handling of toast.* options, and the exact behaviour for equal values from two sources cannot be checked. Only 3 of 17 messages were read directly.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

Peter Eisentraut argued that this syntax is the wrong approach and suggested something like USING (LIKE t1).

precedents_retrieved.title: Create shorthand for including all extra tests
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an 'all' value for PG_TEST_EXTRA, checked through a new check_extra_tests_enabled() function in Test/Utils.pm, so a full run includes every extra test suite. After feedback it replaced 'all' with a 'needs-private-lo' category that enables the kerberos, ldap, load_balance and ssl tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the extra tests are excluded by default because they are security hazards, so each should be reviewed before it is enabled. Peter Eisentraut said 'needs-private-lo' is not the only condition, since kerberos and ldap need extra software and load_balance may need edits to the hosts file. He also preferred each test deciding on its own over a central mapping, and saw no sensible grouping for six values. The author agreed to revisit the idea if more PG_TEST_EXTRA options appear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So someone would still need to familiarize themselves with these tests
individually before setting a global option like this.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reloptions for table access methods
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch passes validate=false to fillRelOptions() for heap tables, so a custom table access method can define new reloptions of kind RELOPT_KIND_HEAP. This skips the second, hard-coded validation step that rejects such options today.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs objected that not all heap options should be common to every table AM, that table and index options should work the same way, and that a behavior change needs tests, docs and code comments. Michael Paquier agreed that bypassing a sanity check is not a good long-term solution and sketched a callback-based design. Jeff Davis said he would withdraw the patch if only a fully supported feature was acceptable, and the entry was withdrawn after Simon's promised longer reply did not appear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The simple patch is admirable, but not something we should put into core.

precedents_retrieved.title: Per-table storage parameters for TableAM/IndexAM extensions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a per-AM routine so a table access method validates its own storage parameters instead of heap_reloptions, letting extension AMs accept their own options. A later version extends ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD with an OPTIONS (ADD | DROP ...) clause so options change in the same command as the AM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry sat in waiting-on-author past the commitfest threshold, so Jacob Champion marked it Returned with Feedback. Before that, the test module failed to build on Windows, and the later patch still had compiler errors in gram.y on cfbot. The author called it work in progress, and no version without these errors appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This entry has been waiting on author input for a while (our current
threshold is roughly two weeks), so I've marked it Returned with
Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
Reverted commit(s): Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables; Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables; Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables; autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables; Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned tables on ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts the following commits:
1b5617eb844cd2470a334c1d2eec66cf9b39c41a Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables
0e69f705cc1a3df273b38c9883fb5765991e04fe Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables
41badeaba8beee7648ebe7923a41c04f1f3cb302 Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables
0827e8af70f4653ba17ed773f123a60eadd9f9c9 autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables

There are efficiency issues in this code when handling databases with
large numbers of partitions, and it doesn't look like there isn't any
trivial way to handle those.  There are some other issues as well.  It's
now too late in the cycle for nontrivial fixes, so we'll have to let
Postgres 14 users continue to manually deal with ANALYZE their
partitioned tables, and hopefully we can fix the issues for Postgres 15.

I kept [most of] be280cdad298 ("Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned
tables on ANALYZE") because while we added it due to 0827e8af70f4, it is
a good bugfix in its own right, since it affects manual analyze as well
as autovacuum-induced analyze, and there's no reason to revert it.

I retained the addition of relkind 'p' to tables included by
pg_stat_user_tables, because reverting that would require a catversion
bump.
Also, in pg14 only, I keep a struct member that was added to
PgStat_TabStatEntry to avoid breaking compatibility with existing stat
files.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add --include-table-data-where option to pg_dump, to export only a subset of table data
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump option (initially --include-table-data-where=table:filter_clause, later discussed as --where) that applies a user-supplied WHERE clause to the data dump of tables matching a pattern, so that only a subset of rows is exported. The option could be given multiple times, and each filter applied to every table matching its pattern.
precedents_retrieved.objection: It was returned with feedback because the patch had merge conflicts and was not rebased after a reviewer asked for it; the author posted a rebased patch only after the entry had been closed. Reviewers had also raised open design points about the option syntax: the use of a colon to separate table from clause, how colons in table or column names would be parsed, and how the option interacts with --table. One participant also questioned whether the feature was needed, given psql \copy.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given this patch has not been updated, I'm marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for partitioned tables. It first creates catalog entries for all partition indexes as invalid, then builds and validates them the way REINDEX CONCURRENTLY does, so an interrupted run leaves INVALID indexes that DROP or REINDEX can clean up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages are reviews and fixes from mid-2024 with no stated objection, and in October 2024 a user asked why progress had stalled; the entry was withdrawn in April 2025 with no visible closing message.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel Inserts in CREATE TABLE AS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the leader and the parallel workers insert tuples into the new table themselves when the SELECT part of CREATE TABLE AS runs under a top-level Gather node, so no tuples go back through the Gather. A second patch changes the planner to ignore parallel tuple cost for such queries so that it picks parallel plans more often.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after measuring a regression with large tuples (about 1064 bytes). Workers extending the relation at the same time spent most of their time in RelationAddExtraBlocks flushing new empty pages to disk. A reviewer measured about 6% degradation in that case. The author proposed waiting for faster relation extension, such as fallocate() from the AIO/DIO work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Upon
further analysis, it turned out that the parallel workers are
requiring frequent extra blocks addition while concurrently extending
the relation(in RelationAddExtraBlocks) and the majority of the time
spent is going into flushing those new empty pages/blocks onto the
disk.

roaster_notes.note: Both objections come from P1's recorded reason. P2 is a revert whose recorded reason gives no detail, so it is not used.
pg_dump does not emit like clauses, so the dump round-trip is not affected. Silently ignoring the option for views and foreign tables follows how other like options already behave.

The proposal only copies existing reloptions into the new table's pg_class.reloptions at create time, so it adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column or wire protocol change, and pg_dump does not emit LIKE. The touched-file list shows a change to reloptions.h, but the material does not say what changed, so whether extensions that call untransformRelOptions() are affected cannot be checked without the code.

No security objection. The source table's reloptions are already readable by any user through pg_class, and like already requires access to the source table. Every copied storage parameter is one the new table's owner could set in a with clause, so the option grants no new privilege, exposes no new data and opens no new denial-of-service path.
Two objections. Demand and fit look acceptable, and several reviewers engaged.

Today a user can read pg_class.reloptions for the source table and its TOAST table, then run alter table ... set (...) or build the with clause in a DO block. That is less convenient but works, and the other like_options (COMMENTS, STORAGE, COMPRESSION, STATISTICS) also copy properties that users could copy by hand. No contrib module or extension does this, and no hook would be cheaper than the like_option itself. The conflict between two like sources and the with clause, and the table-property concern in [P1], belong to the design angle.
Two demand-side objections. Neither is fatal: both ask for evidence or a narrower default.
